Chapter 9: Supporting Others — Using the Body Code with Family and Friends
When you think about the Body Code, it’s easy to focus on personal healing. But what if you could use it to help someone you care about? This chapter is all about supporting the well-being of others—whether that's your family, friends, or even your clients—by using the Body Code in a way that’s respectful and truly compassionate.
Here’s the heart of it: everything starts with consent. Before you begin, take a moment to talk with the person you want to help. Listen closely to what’s on their mind, and gently explain how the Body Code works. Make sure they’re comfortable, and that they understand what you’re offering.
With their permission, you can use muscle testing on their behalf to uncover and release those hidden imbalances. Think of yourself as a facilitator—someone who’s there to hold space, rather than to fix. Your role is to guide the process and offer your presence, while honoring their own journey of healing.
So, what are the main guidelines when you’re supporting someone else? Let’s break it down:
First, always get clear consent and explain what’s involved.
Approach every session with empathy and without judgment.
Use muscle testing and the Body Code map to discover any imbalances.
When you share your findings, do it gently—give the person time to process and respond in their own way.
And finally, encourage self-care, and check in later if it feels right.
Picture this: a parent notices their child is anxious about going to school. By using the Body Code, the parent discovers a trapped emotion—maybe fear from something that happened recently. After releasing that energy, the child feels more relaxed and confident.
It’s not just people who benefit—pets can carry trapped emotions too. Animals often respond well to gentle release sessions, and you might notice them becoming calmer or more at ease afterwards.
At its core, supporting others with the Body Code is an act of service. It’s about showing up with respect, humility, and a willingness to help. And here’s something to remember: you don’t have to do it all yourself. Know your own limits, and if someone needs more specialized care, don’t hesitate to refer them to a professional.
The Body Code isn’t about fixing others—it’s about creating a safe, open space where real healing can happen. Sometimes, just being present and holding that space is the most powerful gift you can give.
